transcription:
Meeting header: 2027-11-09 15:00 UTC | Duration 45m | Attendees: Avery, Diego, Priya — Redwood; Samir, Laura, Nate, Iris — Rivermark.

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, quick agenda — TTFT results, streaming check, kernel choices Diego's been running, and next steps for the dedicated run. \n[00:15] Samir: hey, thanks. quick note, we had a spike yesterday at 100ms p95 for some longer prompts, wanted to see if that's related to padding or batching.
[00:28] Diego: yeah, so we've been doing per-model kernel sweeps, what looks like the NV-friendly fused attention kernel performs well at seq <= 512, above that the cu-based matmul path is more stable. i put numbers in the sheet. (mumble) KV cash — sorry, KV cache — reuse is key, we saw TTFT drop from ~220ms to ~120ms when we warm prefix cache.
[00:50] Laura: are these numbers with streaming turned on? we rely on first incremental token for our UX, that's the main metric.
[01:05] Diego: mostly yes, but note streaming has two components: model tokenization/response and network framing. for TTFT in streaming mode we saw about 80-120ms improvement on short prompts but for long seqs streaming doesn't help as much because the attention compute for the first token still needs the entire prefix kv if not cached.
[01:30] Nate: so does that mean we should increase partial caching or shorter seq truncation? ops-wise we can't always change client prompts.
[01:40] Diego: recommended pattern — 1) aggressive KV cache on repeated contexts, 2) dynamic routing: use a low-latency quantized variant for short interactive prompts, fall back to full-precision for batch jobs. that gives best TTFT vs cost tradeoff.
[02:02] Priya: quick Q — kernel choices: are you picking kernels per batch or per request?
[02:10] Diego: per-model profile at runtime plus a small heuristic: if seqlen < 256 select fused kernel A, 256-1024 choose kernel B with cu matmul path; if GPU is A100 vs H100 it will bias picks. The runtime can override at request time if queue latency goes up.
[02:32] Samir: we tried quant 4-bit in a branch and saw throughput improve but output quality dropped on our reranking task. is there a recommended fallback?
[02:40] Diego: yep fallback to 8-bit for rerank. also you can do hybrid: embed-critical layers in higher precision. we'll mark those in the spreadsheet.
[03:00] [hand off to deep dive — Diego screen shared kernel sheet link: https://redwood.share/benchmarks/rivermark-kernels ]
[03:18] Diego: the sheet has per-model rows, seqlen buckets, median TTFT, p95, and notes on memory. some transcriptions in the sheet are messy — ignore typos.
[03:35] Laura: can you call out streaming-specific numbers? i.e., time-to-first-byte vs time-to-first-token?
[03:45] Diego: sure — in the sheet column 'streaming_TTFB' and 'streaming_TTFT' — TTFB often 30-50ms lower but TTFT depends on cache. for short interactive prompts TTFT median ~90ms on H100 for quantized small-mode.
[04:05] Avery: what's your current sequence length distribution Samir? can you remind the percentiles?
[04:12] Samir: 50th about 180, 75th 420, 95th 1500 — the 95th is rare but causes big tail.
[04:25] Nate: that 1500 is killing p95, is padding the main culprit?
[04:30] Diego: padding and batching together — if batched requests include long and short prompts, everyone pays for the long sequence. we recommend length-based bucketing for batching, and dynamic per-request batch limits.
[04:50] Samir: length-based bucketing seems doable on our side, we can change client to send 'approx_seq' header. will reduce mixing.
[05:00] Iris: any infra changes needed for dedicated? we want to test dedicated A100 pool next week.
[05:08] Avery: we'll need a 2-hour window to spin up the pool and run controlled bench, ideally after hours. I can schedule.
[05:18] Diego: one more note on streaming — chunk size matters. smaller chunks give earlier UI updates but more RPC overhead. we recommend 1-token immediate flush for UI, but group header frames every 50ms to reduce overhead.
[05:35] Laura: curious about kernel warm-up cost, does switching kernels add latency?
[05:40] Diego: cold kernel swap can add ~30-60ms once, but runtime caches kernel choices per device/model pair. avoid frequent switches by grouping similar traffic to the same instance class.
[05:58] Samir: ok — about the spike yesterday, i can share trace logs. we saw queueing at the ingress for ~60ms then model p95 120ms.
[06:10] Diego: upload trace — look for repeated allocation on layer3, might be due to tensor reshape path in that kernel. we'll annotate in the sheet.
[06:22] Priya: any notes on SLOs? do we need to change expectations for TTFT under heavy load?
[06:30] Avery: suggested SLOs for interactive: TTFT median < 150ms, p95 < 350ms; for batch endpoints different. we'll align on acceptable SLOs in follow-up.
[06:45] Laura: can we get a price delta for switching to dedicated for the pilot?
[06:50] Avery: yes, i'll send pricing sheet — rough numbers in the next 24h.
[07:00] Diego: quick follow: for long-tail 95th seqs we recommend two approaches: model truncation policy (aggressive cut) or best-effort degrade to a smaller model for initial token then rehydrate — both have UX tradeoffs.
[07:22] Nate: rehydrate sounds complex server-side. we'd prefer truncation plus explicit UI message.
[07:30] Samir: agreed.
[07:35] Avery: recap of action items — Diego shares kernel sheet, Samir runs a 1s streaming scenario and uploads traces, Avery schedules infra window and pricing, Laura confirms SSO. reconvene next Tue.
[07:55] Iris: quick question — is Redwood able to run the dedicated pool in our VPC for the test?
[08:00] Avery: yes, Private mode with customer VPC is possible, we'll need an infra access checklist — i'll share.
[08:10] Diego: also sending a short note on which layers to keep high precision for rerank tasks.
[08:20] Samir: thanks, that's helpful.
[08:30] [meeting ends — small crosstalk, bye]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (KV cash -> KV cache, H100/Hunt00 confusion), filler words and overlaps preserved. References: kernel spreadsheet link above, streaming trace upload link to be provided in CRM thread.
